reviews.title: Yet another subscription
reviews.text: I purchased paprika several years ago specifically because it was a paid app without a subscription model. Now they’ve upgraded and people can get for free what I paid for and I’m being asked to pay for additional features I didn’t ask for and don’t need while losing out on the money I paid in the first place.

reviews.title: Ugh
reviews.text:
Pros of the huge update: separate cookbooks, so i could move 700+ cocktail/bar recipes out of my main cookbook (although you have to do each individually, at least it’s a once and done prospect)
The calendar feature seems potentially cool. I will definitely give it a try. 
Cons:
You can’t see how many stars you assigned a recipe until you go into it. 
All bloat folders remain in the way of best utilization of the app. (This isn’t new, but I’ve always hated it.)
Typing recipes is a huge nightmare now. I’m practically in tears because every single word needs to be fixed/retyped. For some reason, in the ingredients section, they think you want a capital letter on each line and after each number. Who writes a recipe this way? It looks ridiculous! And they still don’t know that if someone writes 2 tablespoon they want it to be plural. Worse? When you backspace to add the “s” it CAPITALIZES it! So now you have to backspace again, and now it wants to turn the “s” into an “a.” And while the spellcheck was always dubious, now it forces absurd corrections, so there’s even more retyping to do. Please just shoot me!

reviews.title: Here comes the subscriptions even after we bought in

I don’t need a subscription for a recipe app I already paid for. Next comes the updates will not continue to support paprika 3. All these tech companies get greedy and fail. We will see. reviews.title: Lifetime...JK, subscription
reviews.text: You sold a lifetime plan then introduced a subscription. Have you not paid attention to the blowback that has brought other companies? Good luck, but this was a dumb move.

reviews.title: Value Extraction
reviews.text: When I first found paprika many years ago it was a simple elegant solution to the recipe storage /shopping list/cooking process in the internet world. It was so good that when I had to purchase THREE separate versions, Mac for browsing the web and acquiring, iPhone for shopping lists on the go and iPad thats permanently in the kitchen for accessing recipes, I did just that.  That worked great.  And then the developers „improved“ the app and switched to a subscription type service.   I didn’t see much benefit in the improvement but if I wanted to continue using the app as I had been I had to spend more money.  So I bought a lifetime subscription.  Now the developers have switched it up again and want me to pay for service I have already paid twice for.  I get offering new features and charging a subscription fee for those and for any new users but those who have already paid, some twice like I have, should be grandfathered in with the features we had.  I also understand that it costs money to host and maintain software but sticking it to your longest customers is not the way to increase your revenue and appears like a money grab.

reviews.title: Crowded Windows
reviews.text:
I echo many of the other complaints that have been voiced, but my biggest problem is that it’s harder to edit recipes. 

A pop-out window of the entire UI except smaller? Seriously? The previous UI was perfect. Clicking edit just made the fields editable; it didn’t duplicate the entire screen and shrink it down and require futile adjustment efforts. Even trying to stretch the windows out is a pain and doesn’t even help all that much.

reviews.title: Ensh-ification
reviews.text:
Paprika 3, the app I PAID for, had a clean, simple interface that didn’t constantly nag me to buy a subscription. That is what I would expect of a paid app. Now, this Paprika 4 update has forced that exact annoyance onto me and everyone else that purchased the app previously. The developer claims that paid Paprika 3 users were grandfathered in to their “Standard” tier. I purchased Paprika 3 expecting a simple and clean ad-free experience. An application with one purpose, a purpose it used to do well. I wasn’t expecting this subscription-based stuff being shoved down my throat. If a button is locked behind a subscription, it shouldn’t be displayed by default. And the new logo is flat, boring, and horrendous AI slop. 1 star.
Yet another app gone down the toilet.

On top of that, the categories you tag food with are now drop-down menus instead of folders, which makes classifying your recipes unnecessarily cumbersome. All the additional sections in a recipe (servings, cook time, info, etc) that you could just tap into separately are now always expanded and sooo much bigger, it makes for so much unnecessary scrolling and gets in the way. Please let us restore version 3!!!!

reviews.title: The update that removed features
reviews.text:
Update following the developer’s response:

I received a response from the developers (as I believe many other customers did) explaining that importing recipes from social media had not been removed.

Well, here’s the thing: I actually tested it before writing my original review! I tried importing a recipe from an Instagram link and got a pop-up telling me I needed to upgrade to a subscription to use the feature. That is precisely WHY I wrote the review in the first place!

After receiving the developer’s response, I tested it again and, surprisingly, was able to import the recipe. So I’m glad it still works, but that doesn’t change what happened or how confusing this transition has been.

And my original point remains: don’t mess with a product your loyal customers already know and love!

I’ve been using Paprika for years. I paid for it on all my devices, back when you had to purchase the phone and computer versions separately. It wasn’t cheap, but I happily paid because I genuinely LOVE Paprika!

What disappoints me is how Version 4 was introduced. Why not warn existing customers about the changes? Better yet, why not release Version 4 as a separate App Store product, giving us the choice to keep Version 3 or upgrade to Version 4?

I understand that genuinely new features with ongoing operating costs may justify a subscription. But importing recipes from Instagram is something I’ve been doing for years. Being shown a subscription prompt when trying to use a familiar feature

Using the search is made a bit simpler by adding the options at the top of the window, but those options were always available before via a single additional click.  This version seems like change purely for the sake of change.

reviews.title: They just ruined their app
reviews.text:
I have had paprika for a while and I enjoy it. HOWEVER, now people do not have the option to pay once to have the app. Changing the ability to have unlimited recipes ONLY if you pay for a subscription is a HUGE MISTAKE. This is NOT the type of app that deserves a subscription service. It is a recipe storage app. I will no longer be able to recommend it to my friends, and it is why I am writing this review. 

I have 2 solutions for them to fix this problem:

1. Provide a way to pay once for unlimited recipes, like before, but offer an additional subscription if people want the other added features, such as pulling recipes from social media and what not. I can also understand if the paid version limits you to 1000 recipes vs only 50, which is something more reasonable than forcing a subscription. I don’t use the app for the fancy features. I simply use it to store recipes. 

2. Bring back Paprika 3 and leave it just the way it was, and offer Paprika 4 separately for those who want all the upgrades and to only have 50 free recipes unless you pay for a subscription.

The reality is, they have become a company only focused on taking your money without offering any true value anymore. If they don’t change, my recommendation is to use a free document app on your phone and just copy and paste your online recipes to that. It may not be as convenient, but it is more worth your time and money than what this app has unfortunately become. I am so sorry to have to write this review as this

I was a big v3 promoter/recommender. I would have preferred staying on V3 or being given the choice. Not happy about the forced update.

Additionally after the new v4 update they have removed clipboard recipe imports and imports from YouTube videos. They have put these features behind a yearly subscription.

I don’t mind a yearly subscription if it’s new features. However this does not seem to be the case here. Incredibly disappointing.

reviews.title: Get rid of the subscription
reviews.text: I will be switching to Mealie now that they have decided to make a single purchase a subscription.

reviews.title: Another one bites the dust
reviews.text:
Paprika 3 was perfect and a paid, premium product.  The interface on Paprika 4 is dreadful and now we have yet another company who wants our money more often than just the time we already paid for it.

Time to find something else. A shame after more than a decade of being the best.

reviews.title: New layout very, very frustrating
reviews.text:
I really loved this app, constantly recommended it to friends and used it daily. Very frustrating how the list/edit/heart/etc buttons stay on the screen along with the timer. I like using the app in landscape to see ingredients and instructions simultaneously, but now almost 1/3 of the screen is darkened or covered by buttons. Also frustrating that times and the “start cooking” buttons are a distracting shade of blue with no way to toggle off/hide them. 

I love apps that feel “low tech”, with just a few options onscreen, this new update feels like the Paprika team got insecure about the simplicity and bloated the app with useless new features. Would have been better to launch Paprika 4 as a separate app. Extremely bummed and will be less enthusiastic about recommending it to friends.

reviews.title: Never had a problem
reviews.text: Now I guess I'll have to cancel

reviews.title: The death of paprika
reviews.text: I have used this app for years! It’s such a scummy and greedy move by the developers to now push a subscription when we all have paid for this app already. It just leaves such a bad taste in my mouth about them now. Not a good look

reviews.title: Update logged me out
reviews.text: The latest update (November 2026) logged me out. I can’t find my account info anywhere. Bought the app 12+ years ago and my email has changed. I can’t add new recipes and if I buy the app again under my new email I’ll lose 1000+ saved recipes. :’(

reviews.title: Another app ruined by greed
reviews.text: App now has a subscription function that always means paywalls. Not worth it now. To bad one time pay for use is now gone. Time to find a new recipe manager.

reviews.title: Bought the app now they want to make you pay more.
reviews.text: This was the best app, but can’t recommend it to others ever again as now they are trying to rip you off. No thanks.

reviews.title: Ruined by Greed
reviews.text: Was one of my favorite apps and now has been ruined by an auto update that pushes a terrible new interface and subscription based model. Shame on these developers!

reviews.title: No cloud sync without subscription is too far
reviews.text:
Long time user of the app, and have loved it and recommended it to others when it was a one time payment app.

IMO the cloud sync has been so important to how useful the app is to me, I just don’t think I even want to recommend people try this free version. Give people an app they can love with limitations if you want to do freemium. But this isn’t it.

Disappointing to see, wish I could recommend but I can’t

reviews.title: Another subscription, really?
reviews.text: I've been a loyal Paprika user for years and have recommended it to many friends, so I'm genuinely disappointed by this update. Moving to a subscription model without any advance notice was frustrating, especially for those of us who paid for lifetime access. I would have appreciated the option to keep using Paprika 3 rather than being moved to Paprika 4. Unfortunately, this change has me looking at other options, and I'll be sharing my experience with the people I recommended the app to. I hope the team will reconsider how long-time customers are treated.

reviews.title: Another Greedy Company ...
reviews.text: ... which introduced a subscription.

reviews.title: I love this product. But hate subscriptions
reviews.text:
I have been using this for years. I purchased multiple versions of paprika and would be happy to buy an upgrade again. It is fantastic.
But I do not want another subscription. The fact that upgrading now is only a subscription is reason alone to go from 5 stars to 2. If yet another subscription doesn’t bother you, and $10 / yr isn’t much, call this 5 stars.
But yet another subscription bothers me. Give me a $15 dollar one time purchase to upgrade.

To be fair I do not have to upgrade. This is honoring my previous purchases, but now I have a “unlock premium” menu option always showing and the specter of removing features persists (as many others have done).

If it was $15 one time to unlock all the non-cloud features and a $5/yr for cloud features (with a $10/yr option for those who like subscriptions), I would be 100% in favor. Cloud doesn’t stop costing money, I get that.

But only a subscription is not OK.

reviews.title: One of The Most Useful Apps Ever Ruined By Subscription
reviews.text: I’ve had this app since the beginning and I paid a “one time payment” for it, actually, I think I may have paid more than once for it. I have used this app on almost a daily basis. It’s hands down one of the most useful apps I own. Previous upgrades were always free to existing users. Unfortunately, now, the developer is going in a direction that doesn’t really support the users that paid up front and supported this app from the beginning. To me a “one-time payment” means just that. You pay once and whatever features are applied to the app should be available to those who purchased it under that agreement. I was very much looking forward to the scanning feature, which I think I even at one point asked for several years ago. Now putting new features like this behind an annual subscription paywall (not a small one either, even as an existing user $9.99 annually) that competing apps offer as part of a one-time app purchase fee and vs the same apps that are better organized (instead of opening to every single recipe), has forced me to look for a different option. I am sure I will not be alone. So sad this decision was made by Paprika!

reviews.title: Latest release is a money grab
reviews.text: With v3 I could happily import recipes from Instagram reel captions, but seemingly now that's hidden behind a subscription? This feels like a cash grab to take advantage of us users.

reviews.title: Another app I paid for gone free with subscriptions
reviews.text: Was a decent app , now it’s got greedy adding subscriptions i am deleting , I would not of paid for this app if I knew you would add subscriptions down the line

If you’re ok with £15 a year (until the inevitable price rises) then go for this app. I don’t even have the old one anymore due to beta testing.

This includes the basic download recipes from social media function (which was spotty regardless in Paprika 3). 

Admittedly the fee is not the worst out there but it’s still a shame to see something that was quite useful go downhill with an update. I’m so tired of subscription fees.

Not thrilled with the new formatting changes rolled out with version 4 and no option to keep version 3.  What non-cook decided that was a good idea two weeks before Thanksgiving?

Yeah if you previously had Paprika 3 you get access to SOME of those features but not all of them, ie social media importing and calendar sync. reviews.title: Plutôt déçu par rapport aux alternatives

Prenant des recettes de multiples sources, je trouve que Paprika est dans l’incapacité à importer des recettes venant pourtant de site web ou d’Instagram.

reviews.title: Would give 5 star if it allows batch import from pdfs and from safari bookmarks
reviews.text:
I just purchased it and trying the functions, so far I like the concept that you can manage recipes, meal plans, grocery shopping all in one place. A few things can improve in order of priority preferences: 1. I like that they have a native browser where dozens of recipe websites to browse but I wish they would also allow to batch import bookmarks or bookmark folders from safari, and to allow import from PDFs so it’s easy to start using the app. There is “import recipe”in the setting,  further clicking “browse” button takes to the file folder but it would not recognize any recipes saved in pdf format, so not sure what exactly can be imported. It is painful to have to navigate to 100 recipe websites which I’ve already bookmarked overtime on the phone, to be able to save them to the app. 2. For the phone app, the menu bar is hidden and requires to click the 3 lines, I wish they are permanent icons at the top or bottom of the screen for easy navigation. 3. There should be some common pantry items that you can easily browse and select so you can setup an existing pantry in a few clicks. 4. It would be great if the app comes with some existing recipes already loaded, so one can start using the app right after downloading.
Hope these can be added to future updates and I’d gradly change my rating to 5 stars.

reviews.title: App Is Deteriorating
reviews.text: Useful features in this recipe app are disappearing. A prime example is “two column printing.” This feature allowed you to put ingredients and directions on a single page. I work from a hard copy as I find a screen face is too small to easily see. I could adjust the print size and I could put the page up almost anywhere. The one page made everything visible at a glance, saved time, paper and money. I used Paprika 2 in the past and subscribed to Paprika 3 for years. I used to love it. I’m disappointed the developer isn’t fixing issues like these and not even responding to my inquiries about this. Very disappointing! Will likely transfer my recipes elsewhere and not renew the subscription when the current term expires.

reviews.title: Not useful in Canada - grocery lists imperial
reviews.text: Very disappointed I wasted money on this app, the grocery list feature is unusable as it only builds grocery lists in imperial, regardless of if you have converted the ingredients to metric. reviews.title: Could easily be so much better
reviews.text:
One has the impression of a developer resting on their laurels. Which is a shame because there is some functionality which is conspicuously missing.

- Support for websites not in English. I can't honestly believe this doesn't work but as a user I wasn't able to get French, German or Italian sites to work.

- Images are much more important to me than they are apparently to the developer. I want big thumbnails. I want a gallery of images at the very least - preferably a carousel or something. And most of all I want multiple images to be ingested automatically. Images in the present app are a total afterthought. Which is crazy because for lots of recipes step by step images are really useful.

- Play better with YouTube and instagram. Yeah the two places most people get their recipes. And yet neither is more than a crapshoot. In particular, grab the damn poster frame of videos as the thumbnail.

- I shouldn't have to categorise my recipes manually in this day and age

- features like shopping lists and menu planning are irrelevant to me. They are clutter which is nothing to do with a recipe app. Allow me to hide them please.
